sections.h2: Which county handles a High Point house
sections.html:
Most of High Point sits in southwestern Guilford County, while about two percent of its area extends into Randolph, Davidson and Forsyth. The county on your deed determines the tax office, register of deeds and appeal board you deal with.

  • Agent: exposure to buyers throughout the Triad.
  • Private sale: best when someone has already offered.
  • Cash: a fit for a rundown house or a tight calendar.

The city's wholesale furniture market runs each spring and fall and creates short-stay housing demand. Thinking of renting out an inherited or newly bought house? Planning staff can explain the rules before you advertise, and a home occupation needs a zoning permit.

sections.h2: Permits when you sell a High Point house
sections.html:
The North Carolina Building Code requires a permit before building, repairing or altering a structure, and High Point's Development Ordinance adds a zoning permit for activities outside the building code. The city's permit specialists answer questions at 336-883-3151.

Typical zoning permit projects include signs, fences, accessory buildings with every dimension at 12 feet or less, and home occupations. Filing happens online through Accela Citizen Access, and the permit holder books every inspection. The last inspection yields a certificate that the work meets code.

Ask the permit office three questions before you list. Is any permit still open on the address? Did earlier additions get final inspections? Does a fence or outbuilding you put up need a zoning permit? Answers are easier to act on now than during a buyer's inspection period. Copies of permit applications are posted as PDFs, which show exactly what the city requires for each type of project.

When High Point permits lapse
Permit typeLapses when
Construction permitSix months after issuance with no work started, or after 12 months of abandoned work
Zoning permitSix months with no work begun

Clean up an unfinished old project before an inspector finds it.

Guilford County, home to most High Point parcels, made new values effective January 1, 2026. The county did the appraisal in house, drawing on maps, aerial photos, street-level images, sales analysis and field visits. Vehicles and boats are outside it because their values are adjusted every year. The state revenue department had required the 2026 reappraisal in April 2023.

Rates are set separately by elected officials, in June for the year ending June 30, 2027. The county's appraisal line is 336-641-4814. If your parcel lies in the Randolph, Davidson or Forsyth portion, ask that county's assessor how its cycle works.

If you disagree with a value, the first stop is the review board made up of the commissioners. The state Property Tax Commission is the next level. Written deadlines for both appear in G.S. 105-322 and 105-290, and the county can tell you the current filing window.

Good evidence is comparable sales, a recent appraisal, errors on the property card and outside factors such as a flood zone. Collect it ahead of listing, because buyers' agents read the same record.

North Carolina offers three relief programs and each owner may claim just one. The disabled veteran exclusion ignores age and income. The other two, the elderly or disabled exclusion and the circuit breaker, depend on an income ceiling, which is $38,800 on the 2026 state form.

The county assessor takes Form AV-9. Anyone who used the circuit breaker owes the deferred tax as a lien when the house transfers, so request that figure from the county before closing.

sections.h2: Problems that can complicate a sale
sections.html:
Three come up often: an unpaid tax lien, owner financing on a handshake, and a long-term occupant with no lease.

  • Tax lien: the lien dates from the listing date. A county can sue to foreclose it much like a mortgage, and the property is auctioned at the courthouse door. Before the court confirms the sale you can redeem by paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs.
  • Contract for deed: Chapter 47H gives the buyer until midnight of the third business day to cancel, and a forfeiture needs written notice with a cure date at least 30 days out.
  • Occupant: possession under known and visible lines for 20 years can bar the owner's claim, so address a long-time occupant of a vacant parcel promptly.

A title search before you list uncovers these issues while there is still time to fix them.

sections.h2: How a High Point sale moves from offer to closing
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, your attorney searches title, collects lender payoff letters and prepares the settlement statement. Check it a day early. The seller lines should show the loan payoff, deed excise tax, recording fees and any tax still owed.

A cash buyer typically has no lender to wait on, so the closing date depends on how fast title is clear. A buyer with a loan adds an inspection and an appraisal, and a repair request can reopen the price. Either way, settle in writing who keeps appliances, when you move out and who pays utilities until the deed is recorded.

If the house sits on a parcel that crosses a county line, tell the attorney early so the right register of deeds and tax office are used.

sections.h2: Comparing a listing with a cash offer
sections.html:
Subtract everything each route costs you. A listing brings agent fees, repairs a buyer may demand and the months of tax, insurance and utilities while the house sits. A cash offer is lower but the figure tends to be firm and the closing date is yours to pick. Put the two net numbers side by side and choose the one that leaves more in your hands, with the date that fits your life.

Cash Home Buyers can quote a High Point house as it stands, including one with an open permit, a tenant or an inherited title.

sections.h2: What to bring to the attorney
sections.html: Bring the deed, each lender's payoff letter, the latest tax bill, permit records and any lease. For an inherited house, add the death certificate and anything showing who may sign. If a contract for deed or a tax lien is in the picture, bring those papers too, so the title search can match them against the county record.

sections.h2: Moving out and handing over the house
sections.html: Decide early who clears the house. Furniture, stored items and trash left behind can delay a closing or cost you money, and a cash buyer may take the house with contents but should say so in writing. Cancel or transfer utilities for the closing date, and keep the water on until the buyer's walkthrough. Turn over every key, garage opener and mailbox key at the table, and take photos of the empty rooms for your own records.

faqs.q: Which county handles my High Point property taxes?
faqs.a: Look at the county on your deed. Most of High Point lies in Guilford County, while about two percent of the city's area reaches Randolph, Davidson and Forsyth counties, each with its own assessor.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Guilford County value?
faqs.a: Gather comparable sales, a recent appraisal or property card errors and file with the county's review board in its appeal window. Later disputes can reach the state Property Tax Commission.

faqs.q: What building permit phone number does High Point list?
faqs.a: The permit specialists are reachable at 336-883-3151. Applications are filed online through Accela Citizen Access, and PDFs of every form are posted so you can see the submittal requirements first.

faqs.q: How long does a High Point construction permit last?
faqs.a: It expires six months after issuance if work has not begun, and also if work stops for 12 months. Once a project is complete, a final inspection leads to a certificate that the work is code compliant.

faqs.q: Can unpaid property tax lead to a forced sale in High Point?
faqs.a: Yes, through a county foreclosure action and an auction. The owner may redeem before confirmation by paying all taxes, penalties, interest and costs.
